title: Grade 4 HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — Termly Exam #16 (Term 1)

pages.quiz:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — TERMLY EXAM #16 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a use of water at home? (1 mark)
   A. Making rocks
   B. Cooking food
   C. Making the wind blow
   D. Producing sunlight

2. What does water often stand for in religious life? (1 mark)
   A. Purity and a clean heart
   B. Hunger
   C. Anger
   D. Noise

3. Which of these is one of the five great elements? (1 mark)
   A. Akash
   B. Metal
   C. Wood
   D. Salt

4. Tulsi leaves are offered to which gods? (1 mark)
   A. Guru Nanak
   B. Lord Mahavir
   C. Lord Vishnu and Lord Krishna
   D. Lord Shiva only

5. In which faith is the Rijubalika river important? (1 mark)
   A. Christianity
   B. Sikhism
   C. Jainism
   D. Islam

6. Which tree is linked with Guru Nanak Dev Ji at Sultanpur Lodhi? (1 mark)
   A. Tulsi
   B. Sal tree
   C. Bodhi tree
   D. Ber (Beri) tree

7. Which time of day is best for watering plants? (1 mark)
   A. Any time in the hottest sun
   B. Midnight
   C. Noon
   D. Early morning or evening

8. Which tree is linked with Lord Mahavir's enlightenment? (1 mark)
   A. Tulsi
   B. Ber tree
   C. Sal tree
   D. Banana tree

9. Who was Devadatta in the story? (1 mark)
   A. A Sikh Guru
   B. Siddhartha's father
   C. A Jain monk
   D. Siddhartha's cousin

10. What does the word Enlightened mean in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Very loud
   B. Very rich
   C. Full of the light of true knowledge
   D. Very tall

11. In the story of the swan, who shot the swan? (1 mark)
   A. Prahlad
   B. Siddhartha
   C. Suddhodana
   D. Devadatta

12. A snake is often shown with statues of which Tirthankar? (1 mark)
   A. Narsimha
   B. Parshvanath
   C. Buddha
   D. Guru Ram Das

13. What did the wise men say about the swan? (1 mark)
   A. The one who shoots it owns it
   B. The one who saves a life has more right to it
   C. It belongs to the king
   D. It should be sold

14. Which of these is one of the six directions in the Sigalovada Sutta? (1 mark)
   A. Rivers
   B. Strangers
   C. Teachers
   D. Kings

15. How many directions (groups of people) does the Sigalovada Sutta list? (1 mark)
   A. Six
   B. Four
   C. Nine
   D. Two

16. According to the Dhammapada teachings in the lesson, hatred is ended by what? (1 mark)
   A. Silence
   B. Love
   C. Fighting
   D. More hatred

17. Which action follows a Sikh teaching? (1 mark)
   A. Teasing the child
   B. Hiding your lunch
   C. Sharing lunch with someone who has none
   D. Keeping it all

18. How can you learn more about scriptures? (1 mark)
   A. Copy them from memory only
   B. Keep them in a bag
   C. Ignore them
   D. Listen to a resource person or visit a library

19. Who went into the forest with Ram? (1 mark)
   A. Kaikeyi
   B. Vishwamitra
   C. Bharat and Shatrughna
   D. Sita and Lakshman

20. Which is a mistake about scriptures? (1 mark)
   A. Making fun of another faith's holy book
   B. Listening carefully
   C. Keeping it clean
   D. Reading with respect

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain four lessons we learn from the Ramayan. (4 marks)

22. Give two ways water is used at home. (2 marks)

23. Describe how Hindu families care for the Tulsi plant. (3 marks)

24. Who was Sri Guru Ram Das Ji's teacher and predecessor? (2 marks)

25. Tell the story of the Ayodhya Kaand in three sentences. (3 marks)

26. Describe an experiment to show that plants need water. (4 marks)

27. What is the essence of a scripture? (2 marks)

28. Compare the teachings of Parshvanath and Guru Ram Das Ji. (5 marks)

29. Explain how the school can plan a tree planting day that includes learners with special needs. (5 marks)
pages.answers:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — TERMLY EXAM #16 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Cooking food
   We use water for cooking, drinking and washing.

2. A — Purity and a clean heart
   Because water cleans, it is a sign of purity.

3. A — Akash
   The five elements are Prithvi, Jal, Agni, Vayu and Akash.

4. C — Lord Vishnu and Lord Krishna
   Tulsi leaves are offered to Vishnu and Krishna.

5. C — Jainism
   Jains believe Lord Mahavir became enlightened on its bank.

6. D — Ber (Beri) tree
   The Ber Sahib stands beside a gurdwara in Sultanpur Lodhi.

7. D — Early morning or evening
   Less water dries up in cooler hours.

8. C — Sal tree
   Jains say Lord Mahavir became enlightened under a sal tree.

9. D — Siddhartha's cousin
   Devadatta was a cousin.

10. C — Full of the light of true knowledge
   Enlightened beings are wise and full of true knowledge.

11. D — Devadatta
   Devadatta shot an arrow at the swan.

12. B — Parshvanath
   The snake is a sign of Parshvanath.

13. B — The one who saves a life has more right to it
   They said saving life is a greater right.

14. C — Teachers
   Parents, teachers, family, friends, workers and holy teachers.

15. A — Six
   It lists six groups.

16. B — Love
   Hatred is not ended by hatred but by love.

17. C — Sharing lunch with someone who has none
   Sharing with others is a Sikh teaching.

18. D — Listen to a resource person or visit a library
   We can listen, read and discuss.

19. D — Sita and Lakshman
   Sita and Lakshman chose to go with him.

20. A — Making fun of another faith's holy book
   We should respect all scriptures.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Keep promises, respect elders, be humble, do not be greedy for power, love your brothers and sisters, and be courageous (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each lesson.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: Drinking, cooking, washing, cleaning, watering plants or animals (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct use.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: They grow it in a pot or a stand in the courtyard, water it every morning, walk around it and pray. Its leaves are offered to Vishnu and Krishna and used in home medicine.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point, up to 3.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: Guru Amar Das Ji, the third Guru.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the name and 1 mark for third Guru.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Dasharatha was about to hand the kingdom to Ram, but Kaikeyi asked that Bharat be king and Ram go to the forest for fourteen years. Ram accepted calmly and left with Sita and Lakshman. Bharat placed Ram's sandals on the throne and ruled in his name.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three correct points.

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: Plant bean seeds in two tins of soil. Water one tin every day and give none to the other. Compare them after one and two weeks. The watered seeds sprout and grow but the dry seeds do not.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two tins, 1 mark for different watering, 1 mark for comparing over time, 1 mark for the result.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: The most important message or lesson in it.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for a correct meaning.

28. (5 marks)
   Answer: Parshvanath taught Ahimsa, truth, not taking what is not given and not being greedy. Guru Ram Das Ji taught equality, honest work, humility and service. Both teach kindness and care for others.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each teaching set and 1 mark for a comparison.

29. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose a suitable place and get permission, prepare seedlings, tools and water, and give each child a job they can do, such as holding seedlings, filling watering cans or drawing the plants. Care for the trees afterwards.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for permission, preparing, jobs for all, inclusion of special needs, and continued care.
